kamuyhuci: Kamuy Fuchi, an ancient Ainu grandmother of the hearth, deeply lined kind face with traditional tattoos around the mouth, white hair, robes with Ainu geometric patterns, seated with HEARTH FLAMES RISING AROUND HER
kapre: A kapre, a very tall dark-skinned hairy giant seated cross-legged, smoking an ENORMOUS CIGAR with a glowing tip, glowing red eyes, a wide belt, relaxed and amused, isolated figure with nothing behind it
kasaobake: A kasa-obake, an old torn paper umbrella with ONE LARGE EYE in the centre of its canopy, a LONG RED TONGUE hanging from a wide grinning mouth, hopping on a SINGLE SANDALLED FOOT, bamboo ribs visible through the paper
knocker: A knocker, a tiny wizened miner no taller than a boot, wrinkled brown face with a huge nose, a leather cap with a candle stub stuck to it, carrying a little pick, coal-dusted clothes, a knowing sideways look
korpokkur: A korpokkur, a tiny person sheltering UNDER AN ENORMOUS BUTTERBUR LEAF held like an umbrella, wearing small Ainu robes with geometric embroidery, dark hair, holding out a fish as an offering, shy and half-hidden
lamiak: A lamia of the Basque rivers, a woman with long hair seated by the water COMBING IT WITH A GOLDEN COMB, and with the WEBBED ORANGE FEET OF A DUCK below her skirt, river stones around her, a sly friendly look
likho: Likho, a gaunt towering figure in tattered black, skeletally thin, with a SINGLE EYE in the centre of a hollow face, long grasping fingers, hunched and leaning forward, an air of exhausted inevitability
lilith: Lilith, a striking dark-haired woman with LARGE FEATHERED OWL WINGS and the TALONED FEET OF AN OWL, standing upright, two owls at her feet, drawn in the flat style of a Mesopotamian relief, calm and unafraid
lusca: A lusca, an enormous octopus with vast muscular arms and a huge mottled mantle, rust-brown and pale grey, ONE ENORMOUS EYE prominent, arms coiling upward out of dark blue water, suckers clearly visible
manananggal: A manananggal, a woman SEVERED AT THE WAIST with only the upper body flying, LARGE BAT WINGS from her back, ENTRAILS TRAILING BENEATH her cut torso, long black hair, a long thin proboscis tongue, pale and hollow-eyed
mapinguari: A mapinguari, a huge shaggy red-brown creature built like a giant ground sloth, standing on its hind legs with ENORMOUS CURVED CLAWS, thick armoured hide, a single eye, and a LARGE MOUTH IN ITS BELLY
marakihau: A marakihau, a long eel-bodied sea creature carved in Māori style, with a HUMAN HEAD bearing spiral moko tattoos and a LONG HOLLOW TUBE-SHAPED TONGUE extending from its mouth, body covered in carved spiral patterns, deep blue-green
medjed: Medjed, a small figure entirely DRAPED IN A WHITE SHEET like a ghost, with only TWO ROUND STARING EYES and a pair of BARE FEET protruding beneath, faint rays of light from the eyes, drawn in ancient Egyptian papyrus style
menehune: A menehune, a stocky knee-high Hawaiian forest person with broad shoulders, a heavy brow and a thick mane of black hair, wearing a simple malo, carrying a stone adze in both hands, skin warm brown, an intent workmanlike expression
namazu: Namazu, an enormous catfish with a broad flattened head, LONG WHITE BARBELS trailing from its mouth, dark slate-grey mottled skin, small angry eyes, body thrashing in an S-curve, drawn in the style of an Edo catfish print
nanaue: Nanaue, a powerfully built Hawaiian man seen from a three-quarter rear angle so the ENORMOUS SHARK MOUTH SET BETWEEN HIS SHOULDER BLADES is visible, grey shark skin spreading across his back, a cape half fallen away, human face turning toward the viewer
nasnas: A nasnas, HALF A MAN DIVIDED VERTICALLY, exactly one arm, one leg, half a head with a single eye and half a mouth, the cut side flat and featureless, balanced hopping on the single foot, robed in desert cloth
nightmara: A mara, a small dark hunched female spirit crouching as if perched on an unseen sleeper's chest, LONG BLACK HAIR HANGING OVER HER FACE, thin grey limbs with long gripping fingers, enormous dark eyes, isolated figure with nothing behind it
nisse: A nisse, a small old farm spirit with a long white beard and a POINTED RED CAP, knee-high, wearing grey wool, holding a wooden bowl of porridge with a PAT OF BUTTER ON TOP, a stern and easily offended face
nurikabe: A nurikabe, a wide flat WALL-SHAPED creature of pale grey plaster with two small round eyes and a small mouth set low on its broad face, TWO STUMPY LEGS beneath, wider than it is tall, blank and immovable
nyaminyami: Nyaminyami, a river god with the HEAD OF A LARGE FISH and the long coiling body of a snake, scales in muddy gold and green, whiskered barbels, carved Tonga-style patterning down the flanks, immense and slow
obayifo: An obayifo, a witch in flight seen as a floating figure with LIGHT BLAZING FROM THE ARMPITS AND OPEN MOUTH, body dark and indistinct against the glow, arms outstretched, trailing a faint phosphorescent wake
olgoikhorkhoi: An olgoi-khorkhoi, a thick sausage-shaped worm about half a metre long, DARK BLOOD-RED SEGMENTED SKIN, no visible eyes or mouth, both ends blunt and identical, reared up from desert sand, faint electrical sparks
para: A para, a small creature assembled from household objects, its body a WOODEN SPINDLE WOUND WITH TANGLED YARN, twig limbs and a churn-lid face, milk dribbling from its seams, isolated subject with nothing behind it
patupaiarehe: A patupaiarehe, a slender pale forest person with VERY FAIR SKIN and LONG RED HAIR, dressed in woven flax, half-wreathed in mist, holding a small bone flute to their lips, pale eyes, an unsettling stillness
